title: The Darning Basket

doing.t: is overflowing with odd socks
has a wooden mushroom wedged inside a sock
has a needle left threaded with grey wool
has a sock with its hole half darned

close: Just one sock stretched over the darning mushroom, with the mend half done.
Only the darn itself, close enough to see the wool go over and under.

roles.dark: for the gaps in the weave and the hollow inside
roles.light: for the pale wool and the glint on the needle
roles.accent: for the red sock waiting its turn

firstMark: Start with the hole in the sock: one ragged oval of {dark}, no bigger than a fingernail.
Start with the top edge of the basket, a row of short slanting strokes of {main} like a plait.

title: The Library Books

doing.t: is developing a worrying lean
has a bus ticket poking out as a bookmark
is three days overdue
has its top book left open and face down

close: Just the stack, side on, with every spine a different colour.
Only the top book, with the bus ticket peeping out of its pages.

roles.dark: for the gaps between the books and the shadow underneath
roles.light: for the page edges and the sheen on the plastic jackets
roles.accent: for the red spine halfway up

firstMark: Start with the dark lines between the books, one firm stroke of {dark} under each.
Start with the biggest book at the bottom as a long, flat block of {main}.

title: The Enamel Kettle

doing.t: is just beginning to sing
has a chip in its enamel the shape of Wales
is whistling fit to burst
is still warm from the last pot

close: Just the kettle, with the light sliding round its round belly.
Only the spout and the first curl of steam.

roles.dark: for the chips and the shadow under the handle
roles.light: for the shine along its shoulder
roles.accent: for the green handle and the knob on the lid

firstMark: Start with the chips in the enamel, two or three ragged dots of {dark}.
Start with the belly of the kettle in one light, curving line of {main}.

title: The Wellies

doing.t: has a tidemark of dried mud round the toes
is standing upside down to drip dry
has one boot slumped against the other
has thick socks still stuffed in the tops
has a snail exploring one boot

close: Just the wellies, one standing tall and one slumped against it.
Only the muddy toes, near enough to see the tread.

roles.dark: for the inside of the tops and the shadow between the boots
roles.light: for the long shine down each shin
roles.accent: for the dried mud round the toes

firstMark: Start with the opening at the top of each boot, a dark oval of {dark}.
Start with the shine down the front of one boot: leave it bare and lay {main} either side.

title: The Hot-Water Bottle
a: a hot-water bottle in a knitted cover
phrases: that rubbery smell through the wool

doing.t: is plump and gently gurgling
has its stopper screwed down tight
has its roll neck folded down
has slumped over, half full and cooling

close: Just the bottle in its cover, plump and slouching.
Only the knitted cables, near enough to follow each twist.

roles.main: for the sage green knitted cover
roles.dark: for the shadows in the cables and the folds
roles.light: for the raised ridges of the knit
roles.accent: for the red rubber neck and stopper

firstMark: Start with the cables: two wavy lines of {dark} running down the middle of the cover.
Start with the plump outline of the bottle in a light, rounded line of {main}.

title: The Knitting
a: a ball of wool with knitting needles

doing.t: is wound tight and barely started
is unravelling in one long loop
is joined to half a sleeve
has a dropped stitch nobody has spotted
has been batted about by a kitten

close: Just the ball of wool, with the needles crossed through it.
Only the stitches on one needle, near enough to count.

roles.dark: for the shadows where the strands wind over each other
roles.light: for the top of the ball and the sheen on the needles

firstMark: Start with the strands wound round the ball: curved lines of {dark}, each crossing the last.
Start with the ball as one round, light shape of {main}, then wrap lines across it.

title: The Watering Can
phrases: a rose that isn't a flower

doing.t: is dribbling from its rose
is full to the brim and sloshing
has a dent in its side and a freckle of rust
has a beaded line of drips along its spout
has a frog peering out of its spout

close: Just the can, side on, with its long spout reaching out of the page.
Only the rose, close enough to count the holes.

roles.dark: for the inside of the spout and the shadow under the handle
roles.light: for the dull shine along its side

firstMark: Start with the holes in the rose, a ring of small dots of {dark}.
Start with the long spout in two light, parallel lines of {main}.

title: The Wheelbarrow

doing.t: is heaped with pulled weeds
is standing empty, tipped up on its nose
has a spade and a trowel rattling about in it
has a flat tyre that nobody has got round to
is piled high with marrows
has a robin perched on one handle

close: Just the wheelbarrow, side on, with the wheel at the front and the legs at the back.
Only the wheel and the dented nose of the tray.

roles.dark: for the inside of the tray and the shadow underneath
roles.light: for the worn edges where the paint has rubbed away
roles.accent: for the red hub of the wheel

firstMark: Start with the wheel: a small circle of {dark}, with the tyre drawn thick.
Start with the top edge of the tray, one long sloping line of {main}.

title: The Bicycle

doing.t: is leaning on its kickstand
has a loaf and a bunch of flowers riding up front
has a wonky mudguard and a bell that sticks
has a flat back tyre

close: Just the bicycle, side on, with both wheels and the basket.
Only the handlebars and the basket, with whatever's inside spilling over.

roles.dark: for the tyres and the shadows among the spokes
roles.light: for the gleam on the handlebars and the bell

firstMark: Start with the tyres, two circles of {dark} the same size, side by side.
Start with the crossbar, one straight line of {main} joining the wheels.

title: The Old Armchair

doing.t: has a well-worn dent in its cushion
has a crocheted blanket thrown over one arm
is losing its stuffing at one corner
has a newspaper folded on its seat

close: Just the armchair, turned slightly, so you see one arm and the seat.
Only the worn arm, close enough to see where the velvet has rubbed thin.

roles.dark: for the deep creases and the gap down the side of the cushion
roles.light: for the worn shine on the arms

firstMark: Start with the gap down the side of the seat cushion, one deep line of {dark}.
Start with the rounded top of one arm, a fat curve of {main}.

title: The Patchwork Quilt
phrases: a square from every old dress
heavy enough to pin you down

doing.t: is folded with one corner turned back
has a single square that doesn't match
is spread out with every square showing
has a needle still parked in the last square

close: Just a corner of the quilt, six squares and the stitching between them.
Only one square, near enough to draw the sprigs on the cotton.

roles.dark: for the stitched seams and the folds
roles.light: for the pale ground of the printed cotton

firstMark: Start with the grid: a few straight seams in {dark}, a bit wobbly like real stitching.
Start with one square of {main} in the middle, then build the others round it.

title: The Candlestick
a: a candle in a brass holder
phrases: a flame that leans when you breathe
the smell of a struck match

doing.t: is burning with a steady flame
has wax dripping down one side
has just been blown out and is trailing smoke
has burned down to a stub

close: Just the candle and its flame, with the glow left as bare paper.
Only the flame, close enough to see the blue at its base.

roles.dark: for the shadow inside the curl of the handle
roles.light: for the pale wax and the glow around the flame

firstMark: Start with the wick, one short stroke of {dark}, with the flame left bare above it.
Start with the round dish of the holder, a flattened oval of {main}.

title: The Mending Tin

doing.t: has its lid off and cotton reels spilling out
has a tomato pincushion bristling with pins
has a tape measure trailing over the edge
has a pair of stork scissors lying across the top

close: Just the open tin seen from above, every reel and button in its place.
Only the tomato pincushion and its pins.

roles.dark: for the shadows between the reels
roles.light: for the scratches and shine on the lid

firstMark: Start with the holes through the middle of the cotton reels, small dots of {dark}.
Start with the open tin as a rounded rectangle of {main}.

title: The Reading Glasses

doing.t: is folded on an open paperback
is resting on a novel left face down
has a smudge on one lens
is lying beside a crossword with one clue left

close: Just the glasses on the open page, with the words magnified through one lens.
Only one lens, close enough to see the print swell up through it.

roles.dark: for the darkest flecks in the frames and the shadow they cast
roles.light: for the bare page and the glint on the lenses
roles.accent: for the amber flecks in the tortoiseshell

firstMark: Start with the shadow the glasses cast on the page, two faint curves of {dark}.
Start with the frames as two rounded shapes in {main}, linked by the bridge.

title: The Postcard
a: a postcard with a fountain pen
phrases: a smudge where the ink ran

doing.t: is half written and stops mid-sentence
has its stamp stuck on upside down
has a blot of ink where the nib paused
is waiting for a sign-off and a row of kisses

close: Just the postcard and the pen, with the handwriting as loose looping lines.
Only the corner with the stamp, close enough to draw its perforations.

roles.dark: for the ink and the shadow under the pen
roles.light: for the blank space still to fill

firstMark: Start with the handwriting: a few loose, looping lines of {dark}, not real words.
Start with the edge of the card, a light rectangle of {main} drawn at a slight tilt.

title: The Wireless

doing.t: is humming as its valves warm up
is crackling between stations
is playing a brass band to nobody in particular
has its dial glowing amber

close: Just the radio, face on, with its rounded top and speaker cloth.
Only the dial, near enough to read the names of faraway stations.

roles.dark: for the grain and the knobs
roles.light: for the shine on the curve of the case

firstMark: Start with the two knobs, round dots of {dark} pressed firmly.
Start with the curved top of the case in one smooth arch of {main}.

title: The Button Jar
phrases: a rattle when you shake it

doing.t: has been tipped out in a bright spill
is packed to the lid with every colour going
has a mother-of-pearl button shining near the top
has a wooden toggle wedged against the glass

close: Just the jar, with buttons pressed against the glass at every angle.
Only a handful of buttons tipped out, each with its own holes.

roles.dark: for the gaps between the buttons and the shadow in the glass
roles.light: for the glints on the jar

firstMark: Start with the holes in each button: pairs and fours of small dots in {dark}.
Start with a few buttons pressed against the glass, circles of {main} in different sizes.

title: The Spider Plant
a: a spider plant in a terracotta pot

doing.t: has three babies dangling on long runners
is leaning towards the light
has one leaf gone brown at the tip
is sitting in a saucer of fresh water

close: Just the plant, with its striped leaves arching out of the pot.
Only one runner and its baby plant, hanging down the page.

roles.main: for the green of the leaves
roles.dark: for the shadows where the leaves cross
roles.light: for the cream stripe down each leaf

firstMark: Start with the leaves crossing near the pot, a few short wedges of {dark}.
Start with one arching leaf: two curved lines of {main} with a bare stripe between them.

title: The Tulips

doing.t: is drooping in every direction
has one tulip opened wide to show its dark middle
has dropped a single petal
is still in tight green bud

close: Just the tulips, every stem bending its own way.
Only one flower, wide open, with the dark star at its heart.

roles.dark: for the shadows inside the cups and the dark centres
roles.light: for the pale petal edges and the light on the vase
roles.accent: for the green stems and leaves

firstMark: Start with the cup of one tulip, a deep curve of {main}, with the far petal pressed slightly darker.
Start with the shadow inside the open flower, a small star of {dark}.

title: The Bird Feeder
phrases: the busiest stop on the street

doing.t: is still swaying from its last visitor
is down to its last few seeds
is full to the top with sunflower hearts
has a blue tit hanging upside down from it
has a red squirrel helping itself

close: Just the feeder, with the seed showing through and a perch on each side.
Only the perch and the feeding hole above it.

roles.main: for the green metal lid and base
roles.dark: for the shadows between the seeds
roles.light: for the shine on the tube

firstMark: Start with the seed showing through the tube, a cluster of small marks of {dark}.
Start with the domed lid, one rounded line of {main} with the hanging loop above.

title: The Storm Lantern
phrases: a pool of light to walk in

doing.t: is glowing with its wick turned low
has its wire handle raised, ready to be carried
has gone sooty up one side of the glass
has just been lit and is still flickering
has a moth circling the glass

close: Just the lantern, with the flame left as bare paper inside the glass.
Only the glass and the flame, near enough to see the soot curling up one side.

roles.dark: for the soot and the shadows under the cap
roles.light: for the glow inside the glass

firstMark: Start with the wire guards across the glass, a few curved lines of {dark}.
Start with the domed cap on top in a short, firm curve of {main}.

title: The Picnic Hamper
phrases: a flask and a mystery tin

doing.t: has its lid propped open on a leather strap
is packed so full the lid won't shut
has a bottle of ginger beer poking out of one side
has a ladybird walking along its handle

close: Just the hamper, lid open, with the plates strapped inside.
Only the weave and the leather buckle, near enough to see each strand.

roles.dark: for the gaps in the weave and the shadow inside
roles.light: for the china plates in the lid

firstMark: Start with the leather straps, two short bands of {dark} across the lid.
Start with the weave in short, slanting rows of {main}, each row leaning the opposite way.

title: The Long Scarf

doing.t: is coiled in a loose heap
is lying where it was dropped
is still curled into the shape of someone's neck
has a burr caught in one tassel

close: Just the scarf, coiled up, with the stripes going round and round.
Only the fringed end, close enough to see each tassel.

roles.dark: for the navy stripes and the shadows in the folds
roles.light: for the ridges of the knit

firstMark: Start with the inside of the coil, a dark curl of {dark} where the scarf folds under.
Start with one stripe of {main} following the curve of the coil.

title: The Deckchair
phrases: impossible to put up first go

doing.t: has a sunhat left on its seat
has folded itself flat with a clatter
is tilted back at a lazy angle
has a towel slung over the top

close: Just the deckchair, side on, with the wooden frame and the curve of the canvas.
Only the striped canvas and the sag in the middle.

roles.dark: for the shadow under the seat and the joints in the frame
roles.light: for the pale stripes

firstMark: Start with the shadow under the seat, one long, slanting band of {dark}.
Start with the sagging curve of the canvas, one slow line of {main}.

title: The Bucket and Spade

doing.t: has a turned-out sandcastle slumping beside it
has a haul of shells rattling inside
has a paper flag waiting for a turret
has sand caked round the handle
has a crab peering over the edge

close: Just the bucket, with the spade leaning in it at an angle.
Only the turned-out castle, with the ridges from the bucket still sharp.

roles.dark: for the inside of the bucket and the shadow it casts
roles.light: for the sand and the shine on the rim

firstMark: Start with the inside of the bucket, a dark half moon of {dark} just below the top.
Start with the bucket as a plain flowerpot shape of {main}, wider at the top.

phrases: waxed runners, fastest on the hill

doing.t: has a frayed rope coiled on its seat
has someone's mitten left on the slats
is propped up on its end
has runners polished bright from use
has a robin perched on its rope

close: Just the sledge, side on, with the curl of its runners at the front.

roles.dark: for the gaps between the slats and the shadow underneath
roles.light: for the shine along the runners

title: The Snow Globe
phrases: a whole winter in one hand

doing.t: is still swirling after a shake
has a red-roofed cottage under its glass

has a fox and a fir tree inside it

Only the scene under the glass, curved and bright.

roles.main: for the pale blue water inside
roles.dark: for the wooden base and the darkest edge of the glass
roles.light: for the falling flakes and the shine on the glass
roles.accent: for the red roof of the cottage

firstMark: Start with the wooden base, a flat band of {dark} under the globe.

title: The Fairy Lights
phrases: switched on when it gets dark

doing.t: is tangled into one hopeless knot
is twinkling on its slowest setting
has one bulb that refuses to light

close: Just the lights, one loose swoop of wire with a bead of glow every few inches.
Only three bulbs and the haze around each one.

roles.main: for the warm glow of each bulb
roles.dark: for the wire and the shadows around the glow
roles.light: for the bright middle of every bulb

firstMark: Start with the wire, one loose swooping line of {dark} across the page.
Start with a halo of {main} round each bulb, leaving the middle as bare paper.

title: The Alarm Clock

doing.t: is ringing and juddering about
is ticking away to itself
has stopped for want of winding
has been turned face down
has its key sticking out of the back

close: Just the clock, face on, with its two bells like ears.
Only the face, close enough to draw every number.

roles.dark: for the hands, the numbers and the shadow under the feet
roles.light: for the clock face

firstMark: Start with the hands: two short, sharp lines of {dark} from the middle of the face.
Start with the round case in a single steady circle of {main}, then add a bell on each side.

title: The Slippers

doing.t: has been chewed at one toe
is lined up neatly side by side
has been kicked off any old how
is warming up for someone's feet
has a kitten curled up inside one

close: Just the slippers, toes together, with the tartan bending over the curves.

roles.dark: for the dark green checks and the hollow inside
roles.light: for the fleecy lining
roles.accent: for the thin yellow line in the check
